correctness.rationale: The sum-of-squares completion is an identity in normalized real L2. After optimization over independent shifts, the orthogonality of modes with integer frequencies +1 and -1 gives maximal squared aligned mean norm p²+q², with equality requiring within-class alignment. Phase orbit classes parameterized by AB are distinct. Ellipse area and curvature follow from explicit trig parametrization; balanced case has zero derivative at turning endpoints and cannot be a nonconstant autonomous locally-Lipschitz solution by uniqueness. For the elliptic perturbation cross-correlation is epsilon*cos(s+theta), uniquely maximizing at s=-theta. The exact two-mode quotient-distance formula proves 2epsilon input distance and 1 unique-mean distance for all 0<epsilon<1. Exact rational and finite-grid verification ran successfully; infinite-dimensional quantifiers rest on proof, not tests.

value.rationale: The object is directly motivated by current periodic-orbit Fréchet methods: averaging across opposite traversal orientation creates a representativeness obstruction despite identical smooth geometric supports. The full continuum and sharp ellipse-to-segment threshold explain structural nonidentifiability; a concrete smooth perturbation makes the mean unique but shows an exact condition-number blow-up (input perturbation 2epsilon versus output jump 1). This has genuine implications for stability of phase-only mean selection and for choosing an orientation-sensitive data diagnostic. Results are not a parameter-renaming of general mean existence.
